content.text:
I read the structure in four regions, from left to right.

**Left tricyclic core.** This is a 5H-pyrido[4,3-b]indole (a gamma-carboline). The pyridine ring has N at the top, with CH=N and then the ring-fusion carbon. The indole nitrogen carries a CHF2 group. The benzene ring is attached through its carbon (position 7) to the chloropyridine.

I wrote the core as n1(C(F)F)c2cc(-Ar)ccc2c2cnccc12. Checking the ring closure: the indole N connects to c2 (benzo carbon) and to c12, the carbon on the pyridine ring next to the CH=CH side. The pyridine ring is C4a (bonded to N5), then CH=CH–N=CH, then C9b. In the drawing, N5 is bonded to a carbon that is bonded to CH=CH going up-left to CH, then CH to N at the top, then CH to C9b. So the pyridine ring runs C(N5)–CH=CH–N=CH–C(C9b).

Written out: c1(n(C(F)F)...)... The core SMILES is n1(C(F)F)c2cc(-Ar)ccc2c2cnccc21. Here c2cnccc21 reads as C9b, CH, N, CH, CH, C4a, and C4a closes to n1. This matches the drawing.

**Chloropyridine.** The ring atoms are C5 (attached to the benzo ring), CH, C(Cl), C2 (attached to the piperidine N), N, and CH. The SMILES is c1(Ar)cc(Cl)c(N3...)nc1.

**Piperidine and linker.** The piperidine N is bonded to the chloropyridine. Its 4-position carries CH2CH2, which connects to a piperazine N. The other piperazine N is attached to the isoindoline-1,3-dione ring.

**Isoindolinedione.** The aryl carbon at position 5 bears the piperazine N. The imide N carries the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group, drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is assigned.

SMILES: FC(F)n1c2cc(ccc2c2cnccc12)-c1cnc(c(Cl)c1)N1CCC(CCN2CCN(CC2)c2ccc3C(=O)N(C4CCC(=O)NC4=O)C(=O)c3c2)CC1
